answer: Divergent Challenge Ledger. Each identity must periodically sign a random challenge pulse tied to its local history; clones sharing one seed produce identical responses, so the ledger flags correlated nonces as sybil. Honest agents diverge by default. An attacker must run genuinely separate instances, paying full compute and storage per identity rather than copying one, which pushes marginal cost to the nadir of cloning's advantage and removes the opal of cheap scale.
